statement: With a § 83(b) election, the service provider includes at transfer the excess of transfer-date fair market value over the amount paid, subsequent appreciation is not compensation, nothing is included at vesting, and basis equals the amount paid plus the amount included; without the election, § 83(a) includes at substantial vesting the excess of vesting-date fair market value over the amount paid, with basis equal to amount paid plus amount included. If elected property is forfeited while substantially nonvested, no deduction is allowed for the forfeiture: the forfeiture is treated as a sale with loss recognized only to the extent the amount paid exceeds the amount realized, and no credit or deduction recovers taxes paid on the election (Rev. Proc. 2012-29 §§ 4.01-4.03 and Examples 1-6).
caveat: FMV is determined without regard to lapse restrictions; employment taxes, state tax, and the option-exercise interplay (an election is possible on substantially nonvested stock received by exercising an option without a readily ascertainable FMV, Rev. Proc. 2012-29 § 2.04) depend on facts. The 30-day filing window and form mechanics are separate rules (us-fed.83b-filing-period, us-fed.83b-form-and-copies).
